title: Tempo reserve arbitrator: per-route surge quota and invoice appeals workflow
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Problem: Customers using Dedicated fleets run short, high-frequency bursts on specific API routes (e.g., batch inference and long-chat) that cause rapid per-route headroom exhaustion and surprising overage charges. Current surge pooling is global to a tenant or fleet and does not surface per-route constraints, making invoices hard to reconcile and support tickets expensive to investigate. Goal: Build a tempo-reserve arbitrator that enforces short-lived, per-route surge quotas, ties temporary boosts to autoscaling policy signals, and produces structured invoice evidence to support automated appeals. Core behaviors: 1) Per-route short window quotas: allocate small, time-boxed surge windows (e.g., 1–10 min) per route that are drawn from tenant surge pools but tracked separately for billing attribution. 2) Predictive boost pre-authorization: use autoscaler metrics (inflight queue, p99 latency, backlog) to pre-authorize transient boosts and avoid reactive over-provisioning. 3) Soft-throttle handoff: when quota exhausted, gracefully degrade to a lower-cost compatible model variant or queue with informative headers and billing stamps. 4) Invoice evidence bundle: record per-request decision traces (route, surge-token, pre-auth signal, fallback action) into a tamper-evident evidence bundle used by automated appeal/billing-reconciliation workflows. Acceptance criteria: - End-to-end demo where a tenant triggers 3 short bursts on route /v1/batch causing per-route surge tokens to be consumed; invoices show per-route usage and an evidence bundle for each disputed charge. - No higher than 5% regression on median latency for steady-state traffic. - Automated appeal flow created in billing service that can mark one invoice line as contested and refund/use credit within 72 hours via the operator playbook. Implementation notes: - Introduce a lightweight per-route quota table in the routing layer keyed by (tenant_id, route, window_start). Keep retention to 24h for debugging. - Integrate with autoscaler via a new signal endpoint (/internal/surge-preauth) that returns a preauth token with TTL. - Evidence bundle stored in dedicated S3 prefix with SHA256 manifest; a signed reference included in invoice metadata. - Billing service must accept surge-token metadata to attribute cost lines. - Add console UI to show per-route headroom and recent preauth traces (runtime-1.18 dashboard widget). Trade-offs and constraints: - Strong cryptographic evidence increases storage cost; mitigate by 24h retention for full traces and 90d rolling index for invoice proofs only. - Per-route accounting adds cardinality; limit enabled routes via tenant configuration to avoid unbounded growth. - This feature changes billing attribution; product should own communications and opt-in gating for first wave of customers.
comments: 2026-01-12: Kickoff meeting with PM and Billing. PM (Rina Das) outlined business need: reduce 45% of surge-related disputes reported in Jan incidents. Action: prototype preauth signal integration.

2026-01-20: Spike complete. Prototype preauth endpoint implemented in surge-controller (branch: feat/tempo-reserve-spike). Observed false-positive preauths when autoscaler bounce happened; added tag for scale_origin to token.

2026-01-27: Design review with Security and Billing. Security requested tamper-evident evidence bundle using signed manifests. Billing requested invoice metadata schema v2. Added ticket: ENG-934211 for billing service schema changes.
2026-01-30: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/surge-controller/pull/1423 (tempo-reserve arbitrator + per-route quota table). Needs load test results and ops runbook before merge.

2026-02-02: Load test 1 results posted: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/tempo-reserve-loadtest-2026-02-02 — steady-state latency +2.7% median, p99 unchanged. Observed 1.2% additional memory for per-route index under 10k active routes. Going to iterate on retention policy.
Next steps: finalize billing service hooks, add console widget prototype, coordinate product communication plan and opt-in list for beta tenants.
